title: Revenue architecture · Series A vertical SaaS
description: Rebuilt the commercial model for a vertical SaaS company approaching Series A: ICP definition, pipeline architecture, and a conversion system that reduced founder dependency.
problem: The company had strong product-market fit in a tight vertical but a commercial model built for the founder's network, not for scale. Pipeline was unpredictable, ICP was broadly defined, and every deal above a threshold required founder involvement to close.
system: ICP redefinition scoped to the three highest-converting customer profiles. Pipeline stages rebuilt around buying signals rather than time-in-stage. A qualification framework that let AEs triage and advance deals independently. Conversion metrics instrumented for the first time to make improvement legible.
artifact: ICP playbook, stage-gate qualification framework, deal velocity benchmarks by segment, and a handoff protocol that moved the founder from primary closer to deal sponsor on strategic accounts only.
outcome: ICP-to-SQL rate increased 35% over the following two quarters. Deals under the strategic threshold closed without founder involvement in 60% of cases (up from 15%). Average deal velocity dropped under 45 days for the primary ICP segment.
